/loans/fha-loans/: Who is an FHA loan a good fit for?

FHA loans are insured by the Federal Housing Administration, so lenders can offer a low down payment and more flexible credit guidelines than most conventional loans. They are popular with first-time buyers and with buyers who are rebuilding their credit.
Do FHA loans have mortgage insurance?

Yes. FHA loans carry an upfront mortgage insurance premium, which is usually financed into the loan, and an annual premium that is paid monthly. We'll show you exactly what it adds to your payment before you apply.
Can I use down payment assistance with an FHA loan?

Often, yes. Florida programs such as Hometown Heroes and county SHIP programs can be paired with an FHA first mortgage when funds are available and you meet the program's income and purchase price limits.
Is there a maximum FHA loan amount?
FHA sets loan limits by county each year. We'll confirm the current limit for the Florida county you're buying in when we pre-approve you.
/loans/va-loans/: Who is eligible for a VA loan?
Eligible veterans, active-duty service members, National Guard and Reserve members, and some surviving spouses can use a VA loan. We can request your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) for you.
Do VA loans require mortgage insurance?

No. VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance. Most borrowers pay a one-time VA funding fee, which can be financed into the loan. Veterans who receive VA disability compensation are generally exempt.
Can I use a VA loan more than once?
Yes. VA entitlement can be restored after you sell and pay off a VA loan, and some veterans have enough remaining entitlement to buy again while keeping their current home.
Can I build a home with a VA loan?
Yes. We offer VA construction-to-permanent financing, so eligible veterans can finance the lot and the build in one loan with one closing.
/loans/usda-loans/: Where can I use a USDA loan in Florida?
USDA loans are for homes in eligible rural and suburban areas. Many areas outside city centers in Marion, Levy, Citrus and surrounding counties qualify. We can check any address for you.
Are there income limits for USDA loans?
Yes. Total household income has to be at or below the USDA limit for your county and household size. We'll check your eligibility before you start shopping.
Does a USDA loan have mortgage insurance?
USDA loans have an upfront guarantee fee, which can be financed, and a small annual fee paid monthly. Both are usually lower than FHA mortgage insurance.
Can I buy a new construction home with a USDA loan?
Yes. USDA financing works for existing homes, new construction from a builder, and USDA construction-to-permanent loans.
/loans/30-year-fixed-mortgage/: Your interest rate and principal and interest payment stay the same for the life of the loan, and spreading payments over 30 years keeps the monthly payment lower than a shorter-term loan.
Can I pay off a 30-year mortgage early?
Yes. Most of our 30-year fixed loans have no prepayment penalty, so you can make extra principal payments whenever you want and cut years of interest.
When does PMI go away on a conventional loan?

On a conventional loan you can ask to remove private mortgage insurance once you reach 20% equity based on the original value, and it is removed automatically at 22%, as long as your payments are current.
/loans/15-year-fixed-mortgage/: A 15-year loan usually has a lower rate and costs far less interest over the life of the loan, but the monthly payment is higher. A 30-year loan keeps the payment lower. We'll show you both side by side.
Can I refinance into a 15-year mortgage?
Yes. Many homeowners refinance from a 30-year to a 15-year loan to pay off their home sooner. We'll compare the new payment and the interest you'd save.
Can I get a 15-year FHA or VA loan?
Yes. FHA, VA and conventional loans are all available with 15-year fixed terms.
/loans/adjustable-rate-mortgage/: How does an adjustable-rate mortgage work?
An ARM has a fixed rate for an initial period, commonly 5, 7 or 10 years. After that the rate adjusts on a set schedule based on a market index plus a margin.
Is there a limit on how much my rate can go up?
Yes. ARMs have caps that limit how much the rate can change at the first adjustment, at each adjustment after that, and over the life of the loan. We'll walk you through the caps on any ARM we quote.
An ARM can make sense if you plan to sell or refinance before the fixed period ends, or if you want a lower starting rate and are comfortable with a payment that can change later.
/loans/construction-loans/: It is one loan that pays for building your home and then converts to a regular mortgage when construction is finished, with one application and one closing.
Which loan types can I use to build?
We offer FHA, VA, USDA and conventional construction-to-permanent loans, for primary residences, second homes and investment properties.
I'm self-employed. Can I get a construction loan?
Yes. We offer construction financing for self-employed borrowers that uses bank statement deposits to qualify instead of tax returns.
Can I use land I already own?
Yes. Equity in a lot you already own can often count toward your down payment on the construction loan.
/loans/lot-and-land-loans/: Can I finance land and build later?
Yes. A lot loan lets you buy the land now. When you're ready to build, the lot can be rolled into a construction-to-permanent loan.
How are land loans different from home loans?

Land loans usually need a larger down payment and have shorter terms than a home mortgage, because there's no house on the property yet. Terms depend on whether the land is a ready-to-build lot or raw acreage.
Do you lend on acreage in Marion County?
Yes. We finance lots and acreage in Marion County and across Florida. Call us with the parcel and we'll tell you which options fit.
/loans/down-payment-assistance/: How much is Florida Hometown Heroes and who qualifies?

Hometown Heroes provides 5% of the first mortgage amount, up to $35,000, as a 0% deferred second mortgage. It's for first-time buyers (veterans exempt) who work full time in eligible Florida jobs such as healthcare, schools, first responders, public safety, childcare and the military, earn up to 150% of area median income and have at least a 640 credit score.
Is Florida Hometown Heroes still available?

Hometown Heroes is funded one year at a time and often runs out within months. A new $50 million round opened on July 13, 2026. Southern Home Loans is a participating Florida Housing lender. Call 352-622-1521 for current availability, and ask about Luminate Path, which doesn't depend on state funding.
What down payment assistance is available in Florida?

Florida buyers can use Florida Hometown Heroes, Luminate Path from Luminate Bank, other Florida Housing programs (FL Assist, FL HLP and HFA PLUS) and county SHIP programs such as Marion County SHIP when funding is open. Southern Home Loans compares the options you qualify for side by side.
Do I have to be a first-time buyer to get down payment assistance?

Not always. Luminate Path has no first-time buyer requirement. Florida Housing programs are for buyers who haven't owned a primary home in the past three years, but honorably discharged veterans are exempt.
Does down payment assistance have to be repaid?

It depends on the program. Some are forgiven over time, such as HFA PLUS and the forgivable Luminate Path option. Others, like FL Assist and Hometown Heroes, are deferred until you sell, refinance or move out. FL HLP is repaid monthly.
What credit score do I need for down payment assistance in Florida?

Florida Housing programs generally require at least a 640 credit score, and Marion County SHIP requires at least 580. Requirements for Luminate Path depend on the loan type. We'll check your options when you apply.
What are the income limits for down payment assistance in Florida?
Florida Housing and SHIP programs set income and purchase price limits by county and household size. Luminate Path has no income limits.
Can I combine down payment assistance programs?

You can use only one Florida Housing assistance program per loan, but some local programs, such as SHIP, may be added as an additional second loan. We'll tell you which combinations work for your purchase.
Can down payment assistance cover closing costs?
Yes. Most programs, including Luminate Path and the Florida Housing programs, can be used for the down payment, closing costs or both.
/loans/jumbo-loans/: A jumbo loan is a mortgage above the conforming loan limit that the FHFA sets each year. It is used for higher-priced homes and luxury properties.
Can I use a jumbo loan for a second home or investment property?
Yes. Jumbo financing is available for primary residences, second homes and, in some cases, investment properties.
What does it take to qualify for a jumbo loan?
Jumbo loans generally look for stronger credit, more cash reserves and documented income. We'll review your situation and tell you what you'll need.
/loans/203k-loans/: It is an FHA loan that combines the purchase of a home, or a refinance, with the cost of repairs or renovations, so you can finance both in one loan.
What is the difference between a Limited and a Standard 203(k)?
A Limited 203(k) covers non-structural repairs and updates up to HUD's cost cap. A Standard 203(k) covers larger projects, including structural work, and requires a HUD consultant.
Licensed contractors you choose do the work. The repair funds are held in escrow and released to them in stages as the work is completed.
/loans/reverse-mortgage/: Who qualifies for a reverse mortgage?

Homeowners 62 and older qualify for the FHA-insured reverse mortgage (HECM), and certain other reverse mortgage programs are available starting at age 55. You need significant equity and must live in the home as your primary residence. Counseling with a HUD-approved counselor is required for an FHA reverse mortgage.
Do I still own my home with a reverse mortgage?
Yes. You keep the title to your home. You must keep paying property taxes and homeowners insurance and keep the home in good repair.
Do I have to make monthly mortgage payments?
No monthly mortgage payment is required. The loan is repaid when the last borrower sells the home, moves out permanently or passes away. You can still make payments if you choose.
/loans/manufactured-home-financing/: What types of manufactured homes can be financed?
Homes built after June 15, 1976 to HUD code, on a permanent foundation, on land you own or are buying with the home. Single-wide and multi-wide homes can qualify.
Which loan programs work for manufactured homes?
FHA, VA, USDA and conventional loans can all be used for qualifying manufactured homes.
Can I buy the land and the home together?
Yes. You can finance the land and the home in one loan, including a new home that is being delivered and set on your lot.
/loans/builder-advantage-program/: What is a forward commitment in a mortgage?

A forward commitment is a pool of mortgage money a builder reserves in advance at a fixed, below-market rate. Any qualified buyer who closes inside the commitment window gets that rate, no matter where market rates go.
How much does a forward commitment cost?
The cost depends on the rate you choose, the size of the pool and the buyer credit profile. We'll price it against your expected closings so you only reserve what you're likely to use.
Does a forward commitment count toward FHA's 6% seller concession limit?
No. The forward commitment does not count toward FHA's 6% seller concession limit. You can still contribute up to an additional 6% in seller concessions for your buyer.
Is a forward commitment better than a 2-1 buydown?

For most builders, yes. A 2-1 buydown lowers the payment for only the first two years, and buyers usually still qualify at the full rate. A forward commitment lowers the rate for the life of a 30-year fixed loan, so it also helps more buyers qualify.
How long does a commitment window last?
Commitment windows are set up to match your build and close schedule. We'll review your pipeline and recommend a window that fits.
Which loan types qualify for the Builder Advantage rate?
The Builder Advantage rate is available on 30-year fixed FHA, VA, USDA and conventional loans. Ask about construction-to-permanent options for buyers who need something different.
Do buyers have to finance with Southern Home Loans to get the rate?
Yes. The committed rate is available to qualified buyers who finance with Southern Home Loans and close within the commitment window.
Do you work with builders outside Marion County?
Yes. We work with builders across Florida, not just in Ocala, Marion County and Citrus County. Call us to talk about a commitment for your communities.
/service-areas/orlando/: Do you lend in Orlando if your office is in Ocala?
Yes. Southern Home Loans lends across all of Florida, including Orlando and Orange, Seminole, Osceola and Lake counties. Most of the process happens online and by phone.
Can I finance an Orlando vacation rental?
Yes. Investment property and DSCR loans can qualify you on the property's rental income, and our expanded programs allow non-warrantable condos and condotels.
Do you offer down payment assistance in Orlando?
Yes. Luminate Path has no first-time homebuyer requirement, and eligible buyers may also use Florida Hometown Heroes when funds are available.
/service-areas/jacksonville/: Do you offer VA loans in Jacksonville?
Yes. We offer VA loans with no lender overlays and no monthly mortgage insurance for eligible veterans and service members, including those stationed at NAS Jacksonville and Naval Station Mayport.
Which areas around Jacksonville do you serve?
All of Duval, Clay, Nassau and St. Johns counties, plus the rest of Florida.
Can I get a USDA loan near Jacksonville?
Many areas in Clay and Nassau counties and parts of outlying Duval County may be USDA-eligible. We'll check the exact address for you.
/service-areas/st-augustine/: Can I finance a second home in St. Augustine?
Yes. We offer conventional, jumbo and portfolio second home loans, including portfolio financing up to $1.5 million with no mortgage insurance.
Can I buy a historic home that needs work?
Yes. Renovation loans and FHA 203(k) loans can finance the purchase and the improvements together, based on the home's value after the work.
Do St. Augustine homes need flood insurance?
Homes in FEMA flood zones with a federally backed mortgage need flood insurance. We'll help you check the flood zone and include the cost in your payment estimate.
/portfolio-products/: What is a non-QM or portfolio loan?
It's a loan the bank keeps on its own books rather than selling to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac, so it can use flexible guidelines such as bank statements or rental income to qualify.
Self-employed borrowers, real estate investors, physicians, second home buyers and anyone buying a property that doesn't fit standard guidelines.
What's the minimum down payment on a portfolio loan?
It depends on the program, the property and your credit. Call us for the current limits for your scenario.
/loans/hobby-farm-loans/: Can I use a regular mortgage to buy a hobby farm?

Often, yes. If the property is mainly residential and the land is for personal use, conventional, FHA, VA or USDA financing may work. Working farms that are your main source of income usually need agricultural financing.
Is there a limit on acreage?

It depends on the loan. Our lot and land loans have no minimum or maximum acreage requirement. For homes on acreage, the appraisal needs comparable sales with similar land, which we'll review with you.
Does my hobby farm qualify for the Florida agricultural (greenbelt) classification?
The classification is for land used for a bona fide commercial agricultural purpose, so hobby use alone usually doesn't qualify. Your county property appraiser decides eligibility.
Do barns and fencing add value in the appraisal?
They can, but appraisers often give outbuildings limited value. We'll help set expectations before you make an offer.
/forward-commitment-cost-guide-for-build: What is the difference between a forward commitment and a permanent buydown?

They describe the same result from two angles. A permanent buydown is a rate that stays lower for the life of the loan. A forward commitment is the way builders buy it: by reserving a pool of financing at that rate up front for many buyers at once.
Is a forward commitment cheaper than cutting the price?

Usually, yes. Published research estimates that lowering a rate by 1 percentage point costs about 3.2% of the price, while a price cut needs about 10% to give the buyer the same payment. A price cut also lowers your comps; a forward commitment does not.
Can small builders get a forward commitment?

Yes. Large builders dominate this tool because of scale, but a lender can size a commitment to a smaller builder's realistic closings. Southern Home Loans sets them up for local and regional builders.
Does the buyer have to use the builder's lender?
To get the committed rate, yes. The rate lives with the lender that holds the commitment. Buyers can still choose another lender, but they would get that lender's market rate instead.
What happens if mortgage rates drop below the committed rate?
The committed rate is designed to sit below market. If market rates fall far enough, the commitment's advantage shrinks, which is why window length and pool size matter when you set one up.
Does a forward commitment affect the appraisal?
The home is sold at its full list price, so the recorded sale price is not reduced the way a price cut would be. Builder-paid financing costs are disclosed in the transaction as required.
